title: Why Did XOM, COP, CVX Jump To 52-Week Highs Last Week? - Stocktwits
content: Shares of energy companies Exxon Mobil Corp. (XOM), ConocoPhillips (COP) and Chevron Corp. (CVX) surged to annual highs on Friday as oil prices rallied to a six-month high amid growing geopolitical tensions. Brent crude futures maturing in December climbed over $116 per barrel on Friday, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures for December rose to $102.40 per barrel. Last week, Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia intensified, stoking fears about energy security and infrastructure and shipments across the Middle East. Saudi Aramco evacuated its Dhahran headquarters after attacks in the country's eastern oil-producing region. While U.S. President Donald Trump said last week that Washington would not be negotiating with Tehran and suggested further developments could follow soon, on Sunday, he ruled out an attack on Iran this week. Meanwhile, though oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have recovered toward pre-war levels in recent weeks, with the U.S. Central Command aiding passage through the critical waterways, Citigroup analysts have warned that the recent improvement in shipments may not represent a sustained recovery. UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo also reportedly told Reuters that any further escalation could trigger renewed supply disruptions. Brett Erickson, Managing Principal at Obsidian Risk Advisors, said in a post on X over the weekend, “Iran is currently launching missiles and drones at vessels attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz. Despite the preparations from all sides to ready for a full-scale resumption of the war, Iran does not intend to allow the U.S. to use this window to flow out excessive amount of oil and refined products in the meantime.” Exxon Mobil, ConocoPhillips and Chevron surged to 52-week highs on Friday amid the steep climb in oil prices. XOM stock hit a 52-week high of $183.75 during trading hours on Friday, closing nearly 3% higher. COP stock rallied to a 52-week high of $152.77 during regular trading, and ended 3.5% higher at close. CVX stock surged to a 52-week high of $ 233.74, closing up nearly 3%. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around XOM and CVX stocks was ‘bullish’ at the time of writing, while it was ‘bearish’ for COP. XOM stock has gained more than 49% year-to-date, while COP and CVX stocks have surged nearly 56% and 50%, respectively. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Shares of AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) slipped 0.4% overnight late Sunday even as the company sought more spectrum to expand its satellite broadband capabilities, while market veteran Herb Greenberg questioned its valuation despite a steep selloff. ASTS stock jumped nearly 3% on Friday to close at $39.70, but ended the week down 2%, marking its fourth consecutive weekly decline. In a Friday statement, AST’s unit, AST & Science, proposed adding Q/V and E-band service-link capabilities to its 248-satellite network. The links would connect satellites directly to customer terminals, broadening its proposed high-frequency operations beyond ground-gateway connections. The request covers selected frequencies between 40 and 51.4 GHz, plus downlinks at 71 GHz -74 GHz and uplinks at 81GHz –84 GHz.  “This supports a deployment model in which the smallest terminal classes can be used by functional mobile user equipment with varying bandwidths, powers, and antenna sizes,” AST said. The proposed services would require compatible terminals alongside AST’s core connectivity offering for standard smartphones. “AST SpaceMobile’s operations are not solely dependent on use of the E-band; AST SpaceMobile will utilize other spectrum, including the Q/V-band and 700/800 MHz bands, for its user terminals in addition to the E-band spectrum,” the filing said. Approval and interference coordination are still necessary, including protections for military users in certain bands. Meanwhile, Greenberg, a veteran financial journalist and investment researcher, questioned AST’s realistic profit potential despite its expanding addressable market. He noted that shares had lost over half their value over six months and recently hit a 52-week low. “Even with that, it’s still priced as if it’s the hottest thing ever, especially when compared with its more established Satcom peers,” he said. Greenberg highlighted an enterprise valuation of 140 times trailing revenue, versus 38 times for Globalstar, 7.5 times for Iridium and three times for Viasat. He also noted a trailing EBITDA loss of about $532 million. “Drilling deeper, based on trailing multiples, you wouldn’t know that its network is nowhere near fully built out yet,” he said. He highlighted multiples of 16 times estimated 2028 revenue and 324 times estimated 2028 adjusted EBITDA, based on $1 billion in revenue and $50 million in adjusted EBITDA. Greenberg acknowledged that a “sky-high valuation” alone rarely justifies avoiding or shorting a stock, while highlighting high short interest and Fidelity’s warning of securities-lending stress. AST is targeting initial, intermittent coverage before year-end in the United States, Canada, Japan, the United Kingdom and Saudi Arabia, subject to regulatory approvals. Continuous service will require more satellites. “We are moving toward service with the partnerships, spectrum and network capabilities needed to bring cellular broadband from space into people’s everyday lives,” President Scott Wisniewski said. The company has more than 60 gateways deployed, installed or planned, supporting over 60 mobile operators whose networks reach more than three billion subscribers. It targets 100 MHz of U.S. spectrum access and 5,600 activated coverage cells before year-end, up from over 3,000. Meanwhile, its smartphone-focused network has shown peak downloads of 98.9 Mbps, with next-gen satellites expected to reach about 200 Mbps. In Europe, Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Telefonica and Vodafone are exploring a joint mobile-satellite spectrum bid, with a satellite provider yet to be selected. On the other hand, Viasat has challenged an earlier AST overseas-spectrum application as “fatally flawed” over interference and allocation concerns. SK Hynix (SKHY) is considering a special dividend of 16 trillion won ($12 billion), funded by gains from its investment in Japanese memory-chip maker Kioxia Holdings, South Korea’s Dong-A Ilbo reported Monday, citing unnamed investment banking sources. The payout would amount to about 80% of an estimated 20 trillion won in gains SK Hynix booked from its Kioxia investment in the first half of 2026. The company is expected to announce its plans alongside third-quarter earnings on Wednesday, according to the report. SK Hynix’s Seoul-listed shares rose marginally in Asian trading hours on Monday morning, while the U.S.-listed stock was up over 1% in overnight trading late Sunday. SK Hynix said it was reviewing options to return money to shareholders but had not decided on a special dividend, according to a Bloomberg report, which added that the prospect of a payout has helped the stock hold up amid a broader selloff in AI-related shares. SK Hynix joined a Bain Capital-led consortium in 2018 to acquire Toshiba’s former memory-chip business for $18 billion. Kioxia’s value climbed following its Tokyo stock-market debut in 2024. While Bain Capital sold its entire stake earlier this year, SK Hynix still holds convertible bonds linked to an investment vehicle with about a 14% stake in Kioxia, according to Bloomberg. Last week, SK Hynix scrapped plans for a U.S. IPO of its Solidigm flash-memory subsidiary. In an Oct. 23 statement, the South Korean chipmaker cited capital-market conditions and share-price trends behind its move. The IPO had reportedly targeted a $10 billion to $15 billion raise and a valuation of up to $150 billion. The decision follows a sharp correction in U.S. and South Korean semiconductor stocks. Additionally, the U.S. Central Command said on X that the commander of CENTCOM, Brad Cooper, visited the Strait of Hormuz on Oct. 25, as U.S. forces have helped Gulf partners export more than 1.5 billion barrels of crude oil since summer. Oil prices pulled back from six-month highs overnight. Brent crude futures were trading at $114.85 a barrel, down 1.60%, while WTI crude futures traded nearly 2% lower at $101.28 per barrel. Meanwhile, as election season takes off worldwide, Trump reaffirmed his endorsement of Benjamin Netanyahu in the lead-up to the Israeli elections. “To the people of Israel, to those who haven’t seen it, I am attaching the Endorsement I gave one week ago to your Prime Minister, Bibi Netanyahu,” he said in a post on Truth Social. Oruka Therapeutics (ORKA) opens Monday with 16-week results from Everlast-B, its Phase 2b trial of Orka-001 in moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. The long-acting IL-23 antibody is being developed for less frequent dosing. In the earlier Phase 2a Everlast-A trial, 63.5% of treated patients achieved completely clear skin at Week 16, rising to 71.4% at Week 28 after doses only at Weeks 0 and 4. Incyte (INCY) follows with an investor webcast on its ESMO cancer findings and pipeline. Highlights include INCB161734, which targets the KRAS G12D cancer mutation in colorectal and pancreatic cancers, and dual-target antibody INCA33890. The findings come from early-stage studies, with separate Phase 3 trials underway. ESMO Congress continues through Tuesday in Madrid. Iovance Biotherapeutics (IOVA) presents Monday on Lifileucel, which uses patients’ own immune cells to fight cancer, in two previously treated soft-tissue sarcomas. The data come from a Memorial Sloan Kettering-led pilot trial. Summit Therapeutics (SMMT) enters the week after reporting positive Harmoni-GI1 results on Sunday. In the China-based Phase 3 trial, Ivonescimab plus chemotherapy reduced the risk of death by 25% compared with Durvalumab plus chemotherapy in advanced biliary tract cancer. Median overall survival was 14.9 months versus 12.1 months at the interim analysis. Novartis (NVS) reports Tuesday, followed by Biogen (BIIB) and GSK on Wednesday. Thursday’s lineup includes Eli Lilly (LLY), Merck (MRK), Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY) and Gilead Sciences (GILD), which reports after the market closes. AbbVie (ABBV), AstraZeneca (AZN), Regeneron Pharmaceuticals (REGN) and Sanofi (SNY) follow on Friday. Lilly’s results will test momentum in its diabetes and obesity business after Mounjaro and Zepbound helped drive second-quarter growth and the company raised its full-year revenue outlook. GSK reports after the recent FDA approval of Hibsago, or Bepirovirsen, its Ionis-partnered chronic hepatitis B treatment. Beam Therapeutics (BEAM) reviews initial Phase 1/2 Beam-301 data in glycogen storage disease type Ia on Tuesday. Additionally, Benitec Biopharma (BNTC) will present BB-301 findings at the Oct.27-Oct.30 European Society of Gene and Cell Therapy congress. Inovio (INO) has a Friday target date for INO-3107, a DNA immunotherapy for adults with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis, which causes recurring airway growths. The company is seeking accelerated approval on a standard FDA review timetable. The FDA previously questioned the application’s eligibility for accelerated approval. In August, Inovio’s said its late-cycle meeting and pre-license inspections were complete, with cash expected to last into late first-quarter 2027. Meanwhile, Agios (AGIO) closes the weekly calendar with a Sunday target date for Mitapivat in sickle cell disease. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said the company secured a $40 billion financing arrangement to buy advanced AI chips, citing the enormous cost of expanding computing infrastructure. In an X post, that the funding would primarily cover graphics processing units (GPUs). Musk pointed to the company’s investment-grade credit ratings and revenue from Starlink and rocket launches as factors supporting its ability to borrow. SpaceX reported third-quarter revenue of $14.58 billion, up 161% year-on-year. Revenue from its AI business surged nearly tenfold to $7.56 billion. Musk has also set an ambitious outlook, aiming for SpaceX to bring in $1 trillion in annual revenue by 2030. SpaceX stock has gained 1% over the week. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’. Nokia delivered better-than-expected Q3 earnings as demand from AI and cloud customers lifted data center networking sales. Operating profit jumped 35%, and the company kept its 2026 profit forecast unchanged. Despite the upbeat results, Nokia stock plunged over 10% in the week as investors worried it may struggle to turn strong AI orders into sales because of supply shortages, high costs, and reliance on major cloud companies. Rosenblatt lowered its price target on Nokia to $14 from $15 but maintained a ‘Buy’ rating, citing the stock’s post-earnings sell-off was excessive. Retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’. Super Micro Computer stock gained 4% this week after the company expected Q1 revenue between $18.5 billion and $19.5 billion, above the $15 billion consensus estimate, according to Fiscal.ai. Strong preliminary results reflect rising demand for its AI servers, which use Nvidia chips widely used in modern AI data centers. Super Micro is also working with Nokia and Nvidia to bring AI computing to 5G networks and prepare them for 6G. The company introduced a new server rack powered by Nvidia’s Vera CPUs for AI systems that can plan and perform tasks with limited human help. Retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘bullish’. Tesla stock rose nearly 5% over the week as the company delivered better-than-expected Q3 earnings. However, Tesla’s capital expenditures rose 110% to $4.7 billion as it leans toward AI and robotics. Investors took note when Musk said merging SpaceX and Tesla would be a good idea. Both companies have formed independent committees to study the proposal, but a deal is not certain. BNP Paribas upgraded Tesla to ‘Neutral’ from ‘Underperform’ and raised its price target to $420 from $266. The analyst said Tesla’s AI progress has been slow, and its heavy spending has increased investment risks. However, the possibility of SpaceX buying Tesla has become a major factor in the firm’s valuation outlook. Netflix stock tumbled 6% during the week as the streaming giant faces slower revenue growth amid rising competition and as it works to attract more viewers and expand its advertising business. Netflix’s Q3 Revenue reached $12.9 billion, in line with expectations, but the company gave a weaker Q4 sales outlook. According to a Bloomberg report, Netflix users are opening the app less often and watching less content, raising concerns about declining viewer interest. Cancellations remain low, but advertising sales are weaker than expected. The company is spending more on shows and movies and adding live sports and podcasts to attract and keep viewers. However, retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’. title: Berkshire Owns Both Chevron and Occidental. Which Oil Stock Is the Better Buy Now? - The Motley Fool
content: Oil prices are high, which is a relatively greater benefit to Occidental, but what happens when commodity prices fall? The global energy market has been upended by the geopolitical conflict in the Middle East, sending oil prices sharply higher. Occidental Petroleum (OXY -0.16%) appears better positioned to benefit from high oil prices than Chevron (CVX -0.52%). But don't pull the trigger just yet. There's a very important reason you may want to own Chevron instead, and it may help explain why Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA +1.02%)(BRKB +1.18%) owns both. Warren Buffett once described investing as a baseball game where nobody is calling balls and strikes. The point of that folksy example is to highlight that investors don't have to swing at every pitch; they can just wait for the pitches they like. And that's exactly how Buffett handled Berkshire Hathaway's portfolio, cherry-picking the stocks he wanted inside of it. It isn't an accident that Buffett bought Occidental Petroleum and Chevron. It was a conscious decision. And it is important to understand that they are not interchangeable energy investments. There is a notable difference between their business models. Occidental, which most investors just call Oxy, has been focused on growing its production profile. Buffett helped that process along when he assisted Oxy in buying Anadarko Petroleum. In fact, Oxy beat out Chevron for that deal. More recently, Berkshire Hathaway bought Oxy's chemicals business. Berkshire and Oxy have a long history, but the second deal highlights a clear focus on energy production. That's good right now with oil prices at lofty levels. For investors looking to capitalize on high energy prices, Oxy could be a better choice than Chevron. For now. The problem with that story is that oil prices have a long history of being volatile. They rise and fall in often dramatic fashion, driven by factors such as supply and demand, natural and man-made disasters, and geopolitical conflicts. When the event that's driving oil prices higher eventually passes, prices usually fall. When that eventually happens again, as it has every time before, Occidental will be more exposed to the downturn than Chevron. When the Total Conviction signal flashed for Nvidia in 2009, most people ignored it. The ones who acted turned $5,000 into $3,105,454*. Now, for the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. It’s a key player in the $1.8 trillion space race, and with the stock recently sitting 20% off its highs, the window to get in early is closing fast. Chevron is one of the world's largest energy companies. It is what is known as an integrated company because it intentionally has exposure across the entire energy value chain, from the upstream (production) through the midstream (pipelines) and all the way to the downstream (chemicals and refining). That diversification helps to soften the impact of oil price swings. Chevron's dividend, which has been increased annually for 38 years, is the best example of how resilient its business model is. Notably, the debt Oxy took on to buy Anadarko forced it to cut its dividend in 2020 when oil prices plunged during the coronavirus pandemic. That event highlights the more aggressive approach that Oxy is taking with its business. While Oxy's leverage has fallen dramatically since then, Chevron's 0.2x debt-to-equity ratio remains below Oxy's 0.35x. So, even from a balance sheet perspective, Chevron is better positioned to deal with adversity than Oxy. If you are looking for an energy stock you can comfortably hold for the long term, even during oil downturns, Chevron may be a better choice. Oxy's dividend yield is roughly 1.8% as of this writing, while Chevron's is 3.1%. If you are looking for income, Chevron wins that comparison. But it also wins in dividend consistency, given its impressive dividend track record. While Occidental Petroleum may be better positioned to benefit from rising energy prices, it is highly likely that Buffett bought both companies as a hedge against a fall in oil prices. If you have to pick between them, Chevron's diversified and resilient integrated business model will likely be the better buy-and-hold option. A heavyweight in the S&P 500, Chevron jumped during the latest session and now trades above the average price objective set by rating firms. Chevron is an integrated energy company that explores for, develops, produces, transports, and markets crude oil and natural gas. Its upstream business finds and pumps hydrocarbons from fields around the world, while its downstream operations refine crude into fuels and manufacture lubricants, petrochemicals, and fuel additives. That integration gives Chevron balance across the energy cycle, since refining margins sometimes improve when crude prices fall. The company also funds lower-carbon businesses, including renewable fuels, carbon capture and storage, and hydrogen. With operations spanning several continents, Chevron is one of the largest and most closely watched energy sector companies in the world. Chevron's latest advance stood out for a company of its size and steadiness. Shares climbed sharply and finished near their intraday high, though trading activity ran somewhat below a typical day. The stock now sits well above both its short-term and long-term moving averages, with the short-term average itself well above the long-term one, the hallmark of a sustained uptrend. That momentum is notable because Chevron's beta is low, meaning it usually moves far less than the broader market. Chevron's share price has now climbed above the average price objective across rating firms, a sign that the rally has outpaced older forecasts. Fresh revisions are catching up. The consensus leans moderately favorable, with one top-tier rating, a large majority of positive views, a handful of neutral stances, and a single bearish rating. Even so, the average objective has not yet caught up with the stock. Chevron's most recent quarter delivered a dramatic outperformance.  Earnings per share beat consensus estimates by a wide margin and more than tripled compared with the same quarter last year. Revenue also topped forecasts and jumped by more than half year over year, a striking increase that partly reflects a larger asset base following a major acquisition, alongside firmer energy prices. Return on equity and net margin both sit at moderate levels. Full-year forecasts call for strong earnings, and the coming release will show whether that momentum carried into the latest quarter. Chevron plans to apply the operating model it refined in the Permian Basin of West Texas and New Mexico to Argentina's Vaca Muerta shale region, backed by a large-scale, multiyear spending plan. In the Permian, Chevron learned to drill longer wells, standardize development, and squeeze more oil from each acre through better recovery techniques. Vaca Muerta is one of the largest shale formations outside North America but remains less developed. If Chevron can replicate its Permian efficiency there, the region could become a meaningful source of long-term production growth, diversifying its shale exposure beyond the United States. Chevron is reportedly considering divesting a package of mature assets in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico. Older offshore fields often require rising maintenance spending while producing less oil over time, making them better suited to smaller operators that specialize in squeezing value from aging infrastructure. Proceeds could be redirected toward newer deepwater projects and other higher-growth opportunities. That approach reflects disciplined capital allocation: shedding assets with declining returns to fund those with stronger long-term prospects. It also shows Chevron reshaping its portfolio rather than simply adding to it. Chevron has long been one of the most reliable dividend payers in the energy sector, maintaining its payout through multiple oil price downturns. The annualized  dividend yield sits at a solid level, though it has narrowed somewhat as the share price climbed. The payout ratio is moderately high, absorbing a meaningful share of earnings, which leaves less cushion if oil prices fall sharply. Chevron's strong balance sheet and integrated business help support the dividend through downturns, but its growth will ultimately depend on sustained earnings from both existing operations and new projects. Recent rating activity shows forecasters catching up at different speeds. Not every move was positive. One firm trimmed its objective while keeping an outperform stance, and another cut its objective while maintaining an equal weight view. (MPC) surged to annual highs on Monday as oil prices rallied amid growing geopolitical tensions. Brent crude prices touched nearly $110 a barrel on Monday as tensions in the Middle East continued to ratchet up. A series of recent escalations, including attacks on commercial ships near the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi missile strikes on Saudi Arabia, and Ukraine’s strike on a Russian refinery, stoked fears about a further constraint in fuel supplies, sending prices higher. Worries continued despite the U.S. government’s efforts to curtail rising prices, including planned fuel releases and changes to U.S. sanctions on Russian imported fuel. Since the U.S.-Iran war began in February, energy prices have been climbing steadily, boosting energy companies. As per Koyfin data, energy stocks have outperformed the S&P 500 by a significant margin in 2026. Exxon Mobil, Chevron, and Marathon Petroleum shares surged to 52-week highs on Monday before closing lower amid the steep climb in oil prices. XOM stock hit an annual high of $179.30 during trading hours on Monday before closing about 0.4% down. CVX stock surged to a 52-week high of $225.67, but ended the session 0.28% lower. MPC stock rallied to a 52-week high of $493.98 during regular trading, but finished the day nearly 1% down. Retail sentiment around XOM, CVX and MPC stocks was ‘bullish’ at the time of writing on Stocktwits. XOM stock has gained more than 48% year-to-date, while CVX and MPC stocks have surged more than 47% and 200%, respectively. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Retail investors in Sellas Life Sciences (SLS) are floating multibillion-dollar buyout scenarios and steep share-price gains after CEO Angelos Stergiou marked the company’s 15th anniversary with a post about its “next chapter.” SLS stock jumped 5% on Monday to $10.49, snapping three straight losing sessions. In his LinkedIn post, Stergiou reflected on Sellas’ growth from a private startup into a public biotech advancing investigational cancer treatments GPS and SLS009. “Reaching 15 years isn't just about celebrating our history; it is about stepping into our next chapter with even greater focus, drive, and resolve,” he said. He acknowledged past setbacks and thanked shareholders, employees and trial participants, while reaffirming the company’s commitment to patients. “Our mission remains deeply personal, and our promise to the patients we aim to serve is steadfast. We look forward, God willing, to the best chapters that are still to be written with GPS and SLS009,” he added. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for SLS slipped to ‘bearish’ from ‘bullish’ levels a day ago amid a 258% jump in 24-hour message volumes. One user said: “My opinion, Dr. Stergiou’s message was a master-class at reassuring EVERYONE that all is well.” A user also floated a minimum $40 billion valuation. Another user argued for a $50 billion valuation, calling a $247-per-share figure. A separate user proposed a $120 billion buyout scenario and also predicted a share price of $540-plus. Across bullish share-price predictions, including scenarios tied to clinical results, targets ranged from $100 to over $540. Discussing buyout news in case of favorable data, one user said: “If BO news post good data then there’s no stopping this beast (really no explanation required as it could go full berserker mode).” BO means buyout. Another user challenged the lofty valuations and said: “I will be so glad to get out of this ticker when it hits $15 again.” The CEO’s message comes as investors have been searching for potential deal signals in recent months. In June, a filing disclosed changes to executive severance arrangements, including lump-sum payment provisions for Stergiou. For CFO John Burns and chief development officer Dragan Cicic, qualifying departures within one month before or one year after a change of control would trigger 15 months of salary, the annual target bonus, up to 18 months of health-coverage reimbursements and full vesting of unvested equity. Sellas’ conference plans have provided another talking point. The company is listed at Booth 138, with a 20-by-30-foot space, for the Dec.12- Dec.15 American Society of Hematology (ASH) meeting in New Orleans. Major exhibitors include Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, AbbVie and Bristol Myers Squibb. The booth size has fueled speculation about a partnership or acquisition. Currently, investors are awaiting data from Sellas’ two lead programs. The Phase 3 Regal trial is testing GPS, an immunotherapy targeting WT1, in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients who achieved a second complete remission following salvage treatment. Its final-analysis process is triggered by 80 deaths. Sellas reported 78 events as of May 11. Reaching 80 precedes database lock, data review and analysis before results are disclosed. The company also expects fourth-quarter topline data from its 80-patient Phase 2 SLS009 study in newly diagnosed AML, including patients with early resistance to azacitidine and venetoclax. SLS009 is also being explored in pancreatic cancer. Preclinical findings from last month showed 17.9% apoptosis (programmed cell death) in a patient-derived tumor model resistant to Daraxonrasib, versus 2.8% with Daraxonrasib alone. The company called it Broadcom Japan’s first “comprehensive” 10-year agreement covering VMware software licenses, technical assistance and maintenance support. Financial terms were not disclosed. VMware Cloud Foundation will be at the core of the infrastructure. The deal targets three priorities: keeping services available during system upgrades, strengthening security and resilience, and accelerating the delivery of new services. Docomo will use the platform to expand capacity and manage traffic spikes, improve security patching and anomaly detection, and run virtual machines and containers on a common platform. Automation across development, testing and releases will help shorten the time needed to introduce new features. Tan also acknowledged that Anthropic and OpenAI had shown an ability to generate significant revenue from their latest models deployed for AI personal assistants. SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk also subsequently responded, saying, “No crying in the casino,” weighing in on Tan’s concerns about speculative AI investments. However, Cathie Wood's ARK Investment purchased 132,498 shares of the company on Monday despite the selloff. The firm also bought 30,218 shares of CRWV for $1.8 million through the ARK Next Generation Technology ETF (ARKW). CoreWeave reported $35.6 billion in total debt as of June 30, while its second-quarter net interest expense rose to $640 million from $267 million a year earlier. Research and advisory firm Gartner recently said in a report that artificial intelligence infrastructure investments are in danger as concerns over bloated AI capex mount. The firm said that as the commercial duopoly for primary frontier models consolidates around Anthropic and OpenAI, the cash flows to meet that massive computing asset base from neoclouds are not scaling proportionally with upfront costs. Meanwhile, major Wall Street analysts are also taking opposing stances on CoreWeave. MoffettNathanson and BNP Paribas lowered their price targets on CoreWeave, while Goldman Sachs took a more positive outlook.
